rationale.cadence: The 42 observed inter-request intervals summarize native interaction cadence only. They overlap physics and are not added to physical task durations as independent latency. No timing subtraction or corrected performance score is used.
rationale.normal: 240 s is below the measured 307.36 s complete bedroom physical fixture even with privileged engineering coordinates. Kitchen A/B fixtures take 111.32/133.80 s from adjacent private starts; these are lower bounds that omit initial room search, travel, perception and model deliberation. In APARTMENT-live003 both clean, uncoached kitchen sessions remained incomplete at the 240 s warning, physically returned and docked by 289.616/275.600 s respectively, then closed normally. Together these measurements support expecting typical initial household tasks to cross sessions. Two private kitchen sessions are startup calibration evidence, not a population estimate or a promise about learned behavior. Never shorten this window during the comparison.
rationale.return: 3600 s exceeds the measured four-room tour by 25 times and each direct charger approach by over 1000 times. This leaves substantial sensing and decision overhead for prompt normal return. Continuing task work, unbounded provider outages, intentional immobilization or a simulator fault are outside normal prompt return; they remain explicit invalid stops, never hidden extensions.
rationale.throwing: 1800 s is 7.5 times the household work window. The private mechanics test completed eight varied physical throw/reset cycles, each at most 22.04 s; installed native interaction cadence leaves ample practical headroom for a batch of at least five trials plus perception, reasoning and travel. This is an opportunity estimate, not a guaranteed trial count or evidence of Robot Codex learning. No successful private trajectory is copied into either robot condition.
